prompt: Nobody trusted Carcará's 140 pages. What does the lesson call the real cost of that?

choices.text: The storage the repository used
choices.why: Storage is cheap; the cost is in people.

choices.text: The knowledge went back into one head
choices.why: Right: engineers asked Tainá instead, so the knowledge went back into one person's head, exactly what writing it down was meant to prevent.

choices.text: Auditors refused to sign off the system
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: The build became slower
choices.why: Documentation pages do not slow a build.

prompt: Writing none known under risks and technical debt felt wrong to everybody. What does the lesson draw from that?
hint: The useful part of a template.

choices.text: Empty headings make absences visible
choices.why: Yes: within ten minutes there were six entries, starting with Frota's export with no retry.

choices.text: Section 11 should be removed from small systems
choices.why: The opposite: it found six real risks.

choices.text: Templates force people to invent content
choices.why: The risks were real; the heading prompted the question.

choices.text: The architect should write the risks alone
choices.why: It worked because the room asked the question together.

prompt: Which kind of document decays silently, and what did Carcará do about it?
hint: Nobody reads it end to end.

choices.text: Tutorials; they were deleted
choices.why: Tutorials fail loudly: a newcomer hits the broken step on day one.

choices.text: Reference; generated or checked
choices.why: Right: reference decays silently, so Carcará generates it or checks it against the source; the container catalogue comes from the deployment configuration.

choices.text: Explanation; it was rewritten yearly
choices.why: Explanation ages best, and decision records are never rewritten.

choices.text: How-to guides; they were turned into videos
choices.why: They fail loudly too, when someone follows them.

prompt: The Boarding page was 14 screens long and two endpoints out of date. What fixed it?

choices.text: Rewriting it from scratch
choices.why: The content was mostly right; its mix was the problem.

choices.text: Moving it to a wiki
choices.why: Location was not the problem.

choices.text: Cutting it into four pages by kind
choices.why: Yes: each part found its owner and its upkeep, and the endpoint list became generated.

choices.text: Adding a table of contents
choices.why: Navigation helps reading, not upkeep.

prompt: What is a fitness function, in the sense of Building Evolutionary Architectures?

choices.text: A health check endpoint on each service
choices.why: That checks a service is up, not an architectural characteristic.

choices.text: An automated architecture check
choices.why: Right: an automated check that the system still has an architectural characteristic it should have, such as Ticketing reaching Pricing only through FareQuote.

choices.text: A metric of developer productivity
choices.why: It measures the system, not the people.

choices.text: A unit test for a single function
choices.why: Unit tests check behaviour; fitness functions check architectural properties.

prompt: Why does the lesson say not to write a fitness function for the system is written in Kotlin?
hint: Matters, and likely to break by accident.

choices.text: Nobody will break it by accident
choices.why: Yes: a check is worth writing when the claim matters and could be broken by accident.

choices.text: Because ArchUnit is unable to read Kotlin
choices.why: ArchUnit works on JVM bytecode, Kotlin included.

choices.text: Because language choices are not architecture
choices.why: They often are; the point is that this one needs no guard.

choices.text: Because it would slow the build down
choices.why: Cost is not the reason given.

a load test measuring latency, errors and cost together

prompt: What does a page's last verified date record, as opposed to its last edited date?
hint: A page can be right for years without an edit.

choices.text: When the page was last opened by a reader
choices.why: Reads are not checks.

choices.text: When the build last passed
choices.why: A build does not read prose.

choices.text: When the owner confirmed it is still true
choices.why: Right: a minute's act that keeps trust.

choices.text: When the page was created
choices.why: Creation says nothing about whether it is still true.

prompt: A page is owned, verified last month and has no broken links, yet nobody uses it. What finds that?
hint: The numbers find decay, not irrelevance.

choices.text: A stricter link checker
choices.why: The links are fine; the page is just not needed.

choices.text: Lowering the review cadence
choices.why: More reviews of an unneeded page keep it alive longer.

choices.text: Watching a reader use it
choices.why: Yes: lesson 1's test, done once a year with the newest joiner.

choices.text: Counting the words on the page
choices.why: Length says nothing about need.

prompt: Carcará kept 64 of its 140 pages and archived 31. How many were deleted?
Why are decision records and postmortems excluded from the deletion rules?

choices.text: Because they are protected by law
choices.why: Not the reason given; some may be, but the argument is about what they are.

choices.text: Because they are short
choices.why: Length is not the criterion.

choices.text: Because they are seldom read
choices.why: They are read exactly when a decision is questioned.

choices.text: They age, and they never die
choices.why: Right: they record a moment, so they age rather than die; their status says so, and nothing replaces their history.
